title: Crossed Fingers Emoji 🤞 Meaning: Luck, Hope and Promises
description: 🤞 means fingers crossed: hoping for luck or a good outcome. It can also hint at a promise not quite meant. See how people use the crossed fingers emoji today.
summary: The 🤞 crossed fingers emoji means “fingers crossed”: hoping something goes well or wishing someone luck. It appears before interviews, exams, test results and tight deadlines. Less often it nods to the childhood rule that crossing your fingers cancels a promise, giving it a mischievous or uncertain undertone.
meaning: Hope under uncertainty is the core meaning. The outcome is not in the sender's control (a job decision, a flight connection, weather on a wedding day), and 🤞 expresses the wish that it breaks the right way. Sending it to another person works as “good luck,” and adding it to your own plans works as “if all goes well.”

The gesture comes from European folk custom, and is often explained as invoking the Christian cross for protection or blessing. Whatever its true origin, its modern meaning is secular. English speakers say “fingers crossed” as casually as “knock on wood,” and the emoji simply puts that phrase into a picture.

The second tradition is the fib. Children cross their fingers behind their backs to excuse a lie or void a promise, and the emoji can wink at that. “I'll definitely be on time 🤞” often carries a hint of self-doubt, meaning the sender intends to but would not bet on it. The result is a useful ambiguity, hopeful and noncommittal at once.

A newer use treats the intertwined fingers as closeness. “Me and her 🤞” says two people are tight, inseparable, “like this.” The reading is common in captions about best friends, siblings and couples, and it appears in the phrase “locked in 🤞” for loyalty. In those contexts the emoji has nothing to do with luck.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: The usual pattern is a hope followed by the emoji: “should hear back Monday 🤞.” Friends send it as support before anything nerve-racking. It also softens plans that might fall through, flagging that the sender is optimistic but not certain. Replying with 🤞 to someone's news shows you are rooting for them without promising the result.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: It appears under audition announcements, visa applications, pregnancy updates, lottery tickets and sports predictions. Fans use it before big matches and album drops. In captions about friendship or romance, it frequently means “we're close” instead of “wish me luck,” so check whether there is anything in the post to hope for.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Fine for informal hopefulness, as in “client call went well, 🤞 they sign this week.” It does introduce doubt, though. Telling a manager a deadline will be met “🤞” suggests you are not confident. Use it for outcomes outside your control, and use plain statements for commitments that depend on you.

confusedWith.difference: 🫰 crosses the thumb over the index finger, the Korean “finger heart” for affection, also read as a money or snapping gesture. 🤞 crosses the index and middle fingers and is about luck. They look similar but come from different traditions.
✌️ holds two fingers apart in a V for peace or goodbye. 🤞 wraps one finger over the other for luck. The shapes are easy to mix up at small sizes, so check before sending good-luck wishes.
🍀 is a lucky charm, wishing someone luck or celebrating luck already received. 🤞 expresses active hoping while the outcome is still unknown. People often send both together.

avoid: Do not attach it to a firm promise unless you want to signal doubt about keeping it.
Avoid it when delivering reassurance someone is relying on, since it implies the matter is up to chance.
Be aware that the crossed-fingers hand gesture is considered obscene in Vietnam.
design: A raised hand with the middle finger crossed over the index finger and the other fingers tucked down. Platforms differ on whether the palm or the back of the hand faces the viewer, but the crossed pair is unmistakable in all of them. It defaults to yellow and supports skin tones.

faqs.a: It means “fingers crossed,” a hope that something turns out well. People add it to messages about pending results, uncertain plans and good-luck wishes. Occasionally it signals that a promise is tentative.

faqs.q: What does 🤞 mean from a guy or a girl?
faqs.a: Mostly hopefulness, as in “hope this works out.” In a caption or message about the two of you, it can mean you are close. If it follows a promise, they may be admitting they are not certain they can keep it.

It can hint at it. By playground tradition, fingers crossed behind the back cancel a promise or excuse a fib. In texts this shows up as a playful “no guarantees,” but the main meaning remains hoping for luck.

faqs.q: What does 🤞 mean when talking about a friend?
faqs.a: Here the entwined fingers stand for a tight bond, as in the expression “we're like this.” A caption such as “my brother 🤞” means loyalty and closeness, not luck.

faqs.q: When was the crossed fingers emoji released?
faqs.a: It was added in 2016, later than classic hand emojis such as the thumbs up. Before then, people typed out “fingers crossed” or improvised with other symbols.
